source_text: Cur ego non eiusmodi etiam daemoniis penetrabiles fiant? nam et exemplum accidit domino teste eius mulieris, quae theatrum adiit et illde cum daemonio rediit. itaque in exorcismo cum oneraretur immundus spiritus, quod ausus esset fidelem aggredi, constanter: et iustissime quidem, inquit, feci: in meo eam inueni. constat et alii linteum in somnis ostensum eius diei nocte, qua tragoedum audierat, cum exprobratione nominato tragoedo nec ultra quintum diem eam mulierem in saeculo fuisse. quo utique et alia documenta cesserunt de his qui cum diabolo apud spectacula communicando a domino exciderunt. nemo enim potest duobus dominis seruire. quid luci, cum tenebris? quid uitae et morti?
thought_title: Demons claim those who attend the shows
orientation: Tertullian is warning Christians that attending the shows hands them over to demons, and he now gives examples of demonic possession and death that followed such attendance.
pass_a_gloss: Why should they not also become penetrable by demons of this kind? For an example also happened, with the Lord as witness, of that woman who went to the theater and returned from there with a demon. Therefore, in an exorcism, when the unclean spirit was being burdened because it had dared to attack a believer, it said firmly: and most justly indeed, I did it: I found her in my own place. It is established that also to another woman a linen cloth was shown in a dream on the night of that day on which she had heard a tragic actor, with reproach, the tragic actor having been named, and that that woman was not in the world beyond the fifth day. To which certainly also other proofs have yielded concerning those who, by sharing with the devil at the shows, fell away from the Lord. For no one can serve two masters. What has light to do with darkness? What has life to do with death?

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of being open to demonic entry, matching the physical metaphor Tertullian uses.
Preserves the passive imperfect force of the exorcist pressing the demon with accusations.

choices.english: I found her in my own place
choices.why: Renders the demon's claim literally: the theater is the demon's territory, so the woman was found there.
rejected: I found her on my turf
I found her in my domain

choices.term: nec ultra quintum diem eam mulierem in saeculo fuisse
choices.english: that that woman was not in the world beyond the fifth day
choices.why: Keeps the literal 'in the world' for 'in saeculo' and the exact time limit, preserving the ominous tone.
rejected: that the woman did not live past the fifth day
that the woman was dead within five days

choices.why: Renders the ablative gerund literally, showing the act of fellowship with the devil as the cause of falling away.

choices.english: What has light to do with darkness?
choices.why: Keeps the elliptical Latin construction and the stark contrast, echoing the Pauline antithesis.
rejected: What fellowship has light with darkness?
What does light have in common with darkness?

pass_b_english: Why should I not also be open to demons of this kind? For an example occurred, with the Lord as witness, of a woman who went to the theater and returned from there with a demon. And so when the unclean spirit was being pressed in an exorcism because it had dared to attack a believer, it said firmly: "And I did it with good right: I found her in my own place." It is also established that a linen cloth was shown in a dream to another woman on the night of the day she had heard a tragedy, with the actor named in reproach, and that that woman died within five days. Certainly other cases have also come to light concerning those who, by sharing with the devil at the shows, have fallen from the Lord. For no one can serve two masters (Matthew 6:24). What has light to do with darkness? What has life to do with death?

problems.why: Latin 'tragoedum' means a tragedy (play), not an actor.

problems.quote: other proofs have also fallen away from the Lord
problems.source_quote: alia documenta cesserunt ... a domino exciderunt
problems.why: Latin says other documents have ceased concerning those who have fallen from the Lord; it does not say the proofs themselves have fallen away from the Lord.
problems.fix: other documents have ceased concerning those who, by communicating with the devil at the shows, have fallen from the Lord

edits.old: Certainly other proofs have also fallen away from the Lord among those who, by sharing with the devil at the shows, have fallen from the Lord.
edits.new: Certainly other documents have also ceased concerning those who, by sharing with the devil at the shows, have fallen from the Lord.

fixed: Changed 'a tragic actor' to 'a tragedy' because Latin 'tragoedum' means a tragedy (play), not an actor.

Changed 'other proofs have also fallen away from the Lord' to 'other documents have also ceased concerning those who... have fallen from the Lord' because Latin 'documenta cesserunt' means documents have ceased, and the falling away from the Lord applies to the people, not the proofs.

problems.quote: Certainly other documents have also ceased concerning those who
problems.why: 'Documents have ceased' is nonsense; likely means 'documents have survived' or 'cases have ceased' (died)?
problems.fix: Correct: 'Other cases have also come to light' or 'documents have also been preserved'.

problems.quote: I did it most justly: I found her in my own place
problems.why: Demon's claim; 'most justly' is strong but context suggests 'with good right' or 'rightfully'; tone may need marking.
problems.fix: Keep but note as demonic claim.

problems.quote: Why should I not also be penetrable to demons of this kind?
problems.why: 'Penetrable' is an odd word choice that does not clearly convey the intended meaning.
problems.fix: Read 'Why should I not also be vulnerable to demons of this kind?'

edits.old: Why should I not also be penetrable to demons of this kind?
edits.new: Why should I not also be vulnerable to demons of this kind?

edits.old: Certainly other documents have also ceased concerning those who
edits.new: Certainly other cases have also come to light concerning those who

fixed: 'Penetrable' is an odd word choice; source 'penetrabiles' means 'penetrable/vulnerable to penetration'; 'vulnerable' is clearer.
'Documents have ceased' misreads 'documenta cesserunt'; 'documenta' here means 'proofs/examples/cases', and 'cesserunt' means 'have yielded/come to light', not 'ceased'.
Demon's claim 'iustissime feci' is correctly rendered as 'I did it most justly'; no change needed.

problems.quote: that woman was not in the world beyond the fifth day
problems.why: 'Not in the world' = died; euphemism may mislead.

edits.old: and that that woman was not in the world beyond the fifth day
edits.new: and that that woman died within five days

fixed: The source 'nec ultra quintum diem eam mulierem in saeculo fuisse' literally means 'that that woman was not in the world beyond the fifth day,' which is a euphemism for death. The English 'was not in the world beyond the fifth day' is a literal rendering that may mislead; clarified to 'died within five days.'

last_rejected.quote: Certainly other documents have also ceased concerning those who
last_rejected.source_quote: quo utique et alia documenta cesserunt de his
last_rejected.why: 'cesserunt' means 'yielded' or 'gave way' here, not 'ceased'; the other examples yielded to (were surpassed by) this one.
last_rejected.fix: To this, certainly, other examples have also yielded, concerning those who
last_rejected.ruling: cēssērunt here means 'have ceased' (stopped), fitting context; 'yielded' is not supported by Latin usage

last_rejected.quote: with the actor named in reproach
last_rejected.why: Latin says the tragedy (tragoedo) is named in reproach, not an actor.
last_rejected.fix: with the tragedy named in reproach
last_rejected.ruling: tragoedus means tragic actor/performer, not the play itself; 'actor' is within normal range

polish.changed: Clarified the demon's claim as 'with good right' rather than 'most justly,' replaced the odd 'penetrable' with 'open to,' and smoothed the sentence about other cases so the meaning is clear: cases have come to light, not 'ceased.'
